how_to_read.flagged: true means the entry is flagged for review, false means it passes
how_to_read.flags_include: deterministic flags that must be present
how_to_read.reads_naturally: low means below the threshold, high means at or above it
how_to_read.note_publishable: low means below the threshold, high means at or above it
how_to_read.theme_kind: the exact choice key Jev must return

notes: Rows 1 to 3 take their gear text from set-season-30-35-themes.js (resolved at run time, Tight End venue). Rows 4 to 8 are synthetic entries; their dates are placeholders chosen only to be unique.

Row 5: the entry's type is Championship and the theme is 'Championship Night'. The deterministic theme-equals-type check only fires when the two strings match, and these do not, so only theme_kind is asserted. The match case is covered by a unit test.

KNOWN CONFLICT IN THE BRIEF, found while writing this file and before any live call: rows 1 and 2 are expected to pass, but the gear text for Flannel and Hoodies in set-season-30-35-themes.js also contains an em dash, and the brief's own deterministic rule flags an em dash anywhere in theme, gear or note. Rows 1 and 2 are therefore recorded exactly as the brief states them (flagged: false) and will score as not met on the dash flag even if every model answer is good. That outcome is the rule working, not the tool failing. Whether to amend the expectation or fix the gear text is the orchestrator's and the owner's call.

2026-10-02: note_publishable wording changed after the first live run scored a plainly publishable note at 0.32; the new wording was probed live on 4 publishable and 3 unpublishable notes before being applied (see research/jev-integration-2026-10-02/SMOKE_RESULTS.md).
